issues.description: The problem statement (UML) and the solution expect Stock to provide a method named addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient), but the template Stock class instead defines addItem(StockIngredient). This name/signature mismatch will confuse students and cause compilation errors when they implement SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery (which the spec describes as adding a new StockIngredient to the stock).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template Stock API match the UML/spec and solution by renaming addItem(StockIngredient) to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) (or add an addToStockIngredients method that delegates to addItem). Ensure the method name and signature are consistent across the problem statement, template, and tests.

issues.description: The problem statement and class diagram require Stock.addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) but the template Stock class provides a method named addItem(StockIngredient). The reference implementation (solution) uses addToStockIngredients. This inconsistent naming (addItem vs addToStockIngredients) across artifacts can mislead students: the task description and solution expect addToStockIngredients while the starter code only exposes addItem, causing compilation confusion or incorrect method usage when implementing SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template method addItem(StockIngredient) to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) (or add a forwarding method addToStockIngredients that delegates to addItem) so the starter code matches the problem statement and the solution. This will align the API across problem, template, and solution and remove student confusion.
